4.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicants submits that the instant proceedings are arising out of the matrimonial dispute between the applicant no.1 and the opposite party and due to which all the family members were implicated.

However, now the parties have settled their dispute amicably and compromise was arrived at between the parties, thereupon, a petition under Section 13-B of the Hindu Marriage Act, has been filed by the applicants before the Principal Judge, Family Court, Agra,
which has been decreed vide judgement and order dated 11.07.2024 and the marriage between the applicant no. 1 and the opposite party no.2 has already been dissolved and as per the terms of the settlement arrived at between the parties, which are narrated in paragraph nos. 5, 6 7 & 8 of the 13-B application, the parties have settled their claims and towards one time settlement an amount of Rs. 7,20,000/-, has been duly paid and the parties have agreed to withdraw all the proceedings against each other, which are mentioned in para 7 of the 13-B Application.

Since, the aforesaid compromise has already been acted upon between the parties and the 13-B application has already been decreed, therefore, learned counsel for the applicants seeks quashing of the entire proceedings of the instant case.

5. Learned counsel for the opposite party no.2 does not dispute the aforesaid facts and submits that the entire amount which has was to be received by the opposite party no.2 has already been received and the decree of dissolution of marriage has already been passed by the family court concerned and he has no objection in quashing of the proceedings of the instant case, in view of the settlement which has been acted upon by the parties.

6. Learned A.G.A for the State also submits that in view of the compromise between the parties and on the petition under Section 13-B of the Hindu Marriage Act, it is apparent that the compromise between the parties has already been acted upon, therefore, learned A.G.A. does not oppose the prayer for quashing in view of such settlement between the parties.
7. Having heard the rival submissions made by learned counsels for the parties, this Court has carefully gone through the record of the case.

From the record of the case, it is apparent that the instant application was filed by the opposite party no.2 against the applicants herein as a Complaint Case No. 38 of 2020, wherein vide order dated 24.08.2022, the applicants herein were summoned.

Subsequently, thereto it appears that the compromise has been arrived at between the parties and an application under Section 13-B of the Hindu Marriage Act being petition no. 6 of 2024, was moved jointly by the applicant no.1 and the opposite party no.2 and in terms of para 5 of the said petition under Section 13-B, the entire payment has been received by the opposite party no.2 and in para 7 of the said petition, the parties have agreed to withdraw all the proceedings against each other.

From the perusal of 13-B application, which has been filed as Annexure SA-1 to the supplementary affidavit filed today in Court, the parties have agreed to withdraw all the proceedings pending against each other.

sentences.text:
In view of the compromise between the parties has already been acted upon, the decree of dissolution of marriage has already passed by the Family Court concerned on 11.07.2024, therefore,
no fruitful purpose will be served by keeping the instant criminal proceedings pending against the applicants herein and by the aforesaid settlement, which has already been acted upon, there shall be peace in the family member as well as in the society.

9. In view thereof and in the light of the judgements of the Apex Court in Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab and Another : (2012) 10 SCC 303; Prabatbhai Aahir Alias Prabatbhai Bhimsinghbhai Karmur and others vs. State of Gujarat and Another : (2017) 9 SCC 641; Narinder Singh & Ors. vs.
State of Punjab : (2014) 6 SCC 466 and B.S.Joshi and Other vs. State of Haryana and Another :
(2003)4 SCC 67, the instant application is allowed and the entire proceedings in Complaint Case No.
38 of 2020 (Smt. Neelam vs. Pawan Kumar and Others), under Section 498A, 323 I.P.C. and under Section 3/4 of the D.P. Act, P.S.- Shamshabad, District- Agra, pending in the court of learned Judicial Magistrate, Agra, are hereby quashed.
